ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a horizontal conveyor belt device, with rollers on the left and right, and the upper conveyor belt is horizontal. The block is initially at point A on the left side, and a dashed box on the right marks the position of point B. From A to B is a horizontal displacement along the direction of the conveyor belt; the arrow in the figure points to the right, indicating that the conveyor belt moves to the right. Reasoning: The problem gives the conveyor belt speed v=2 m/s, the block mass m=1 kg, the coefficient of kinetic friction μ=0.2, the initial velocity of the block is 0, AB=2 m, and g=10 m/s². When the block is just placed on the conveyor belt, it slides to the left relative to the conveyor belt, so it is subjected to a rightward sliding friction force from the conveyor belt, with magnitude f=μmg=0.2×1×10=2 N, and acceleration a=f/m=2 m/s². The displacement required for the block to accelerate from rest to the conveyor belt speed 2 m/s is s=v²/(2a)=2²/(2×2)=1 m. Since 1 m < AB=2 m, the block has already reached the same speed as the conveyor belt before reaching B. After that there is no relative sliding, and in the horizontal uniform-speed state the friction force no longer does work. Therefore, when it reaches point B, the block's speed is 2 m/s. Gravity and the supporting force do no work, and the work done by the conveyor belt on the block equals the increase in the block's kinetic energy: W=1/2 mv²-0=1/2×1×2²=2 J.

After that there is no relative sliding, and in the horizontal uniform-speed state the friction force no longer does work. Therefore, when it reaches point B, the block's speed is 2 m/s. Gravity and the supporting force do no work, and the work done by the conveyor belt on the block equals the increase in the block's kinetic energy: W=1/2 mv²-0=1/2×1×2²=2 J.
